name: scores-display-visual
description: Visual verification of the four score bars in the HUD: Worker Well-being, Safety, Ecology, and Neighbor Nuisance scores (0-100). Verifies scores are visible, values update over time with decay, and the scores command reflects current state.

steps.description: #553: switched from `campaign start level:dusty_hollow` -- dusty_hollow's own terrain snapped a fresh hire/vehicle purchase's grid-centre spawn (findNearestReachableCell, blocked by relief terrain at the literal centre) to a reachable cell over 60 tiles from this file's drill site, which stalled the driller in permanent collapse/rest cycling and never let a single hole land (sandbox-measured, worker_revolt by tick 400 with zero progress). new_game's flat desert_badlands terrain has no such obstruction. Cash bumped to $150,000 (from dusty_hollow's $50,000) for the drill_rig ($35,000) this file now needs on top of its existing hire/building spend.

Hire crew and build the two score-linked buildings the scenario had no way to demonstrate decay without: management_office (safety +2/tick) and living_quarters (well-being +2/tick), plus a small blast below (immediate vibration hit to ecology/nuisance) — otherwise all four gauges sit flat at their neutral 50 default for the whole run.
#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed a vehicle at all) now needs one.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

#601-followup: a solo driller has too little fatigue margin for this file's 4-hole grid to reliably finish both drilling (vehicle-driven) and charging (on foot, no vehicle gate, so slower and more fatiguing per hole) back to back -- direct sandbox trace: even from the closest living_quarters placement that stays clear of every hole tile (`at:17,21` below, replacing the old `at:22,21` which silently overlapped one hole -- see that step's own note), command mode's own deterministic charge phase still stalled at 2/4 charged after 3000 ticks. A second driller with an independent rig halves each employee's share of the same workload, restoring the margin distance alone can no longer buy once living_quarters can no longer sit on top of a hole to shortcut the trip.

#921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.

Crews drill_rig #2 with driller #2, same reasoning as the step above. #921: Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls removed; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one, so this step runs as a direct bootstrap primitive instead of a click.

#601-followup: relocated again, from (22,21) to (17,21) -- (22,21) was never actually clear of every hole cell as #554's own description claimed. living_quarters' footprint (`rect(3,3)`, BuildingDefs.ts) is anchored at its own top-left corner (`building.x + dx`, Building.ts), not centered, so `at:22,21` occupies x:[22,24] z:[21,23] -- which contains (23,23), one of this file's own 4 drill holes (the 2x2 grid at spacing 4 from (20,20) lands corners at (20,20)/(23,20)/(20,23)/(23,23)). A drill_rig can never actually reach a hole a building is standing on: #554's own diagnostic (still 1-4 ordered after 6000 ticks) was this exact bug already, misread as a fatigue/travel-distance problem and "fixed" by moving closer -- which happened to leave 3 of 4 holes clear by coincidence, not by the equidistant-from-every-corner reasoning the old description claimed. Confirmed directly: `wait_until field:orderedHoleCount equals:0` (the deterministic replacement for the old real-time-driven wait, see below) stalls at exactly 1 forever regardless of maxTicks (still stuck after 5000 ticks, sandbox-measured) with EITHER one driller or two drillers with independent rigs -- decisive against a fatigue-margin theory, since two independent crews sharing the same 4 holes would have trivially finished a merely-slow job. (17,21) sits entirely outside the (20,20)-(23,23) hole bounding box (its own footprint is x:[17,19] z:[21,23], nearest-tile distance to any hole at most ~4.1) -- clear of every hole like (22,21) was meant to be, but close enough that the charge phase below (on foot, no vehicle gate) keeps the same short rest trips #554's original relocation was actually chasing.
Let the queued construction site(s) be walked to and built out (#556): ordering a building no longer places it, so everything below that needs a standing building waits here first.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:4 depth:6 start:20,20
steps.description: Four holes at minimal spacing/stemming (vs. the wider, well-stemmed grids used elsewhere) so their energy overlaps enough to actually throw fragments (isProjection) — a single lightly-charged hole clears rock cleanly with zero projections and never moves Ecology/Nuisance at all.

#601-followup: replaces #553/#554's own hand-tuned 5x tick-10/event-choose-0 chunked pad (50 ticks, a "comfortable margin" over a sandbox-measured 47-tick convergence that still occasionally landed one hole short in real CI, "orderedHoleCount should be 0 but is 1") with a real `waitUntil`. That margin was guessing at a number that didn't need guessing: #601 fixed `waitUntil` itself (both modes now loop the console's own `tick 1`, auto-resolving a pending event each time, exactly like command mode's own `runWaitUntil`), so this converges on the exact tick each mode's own drilling actually finishes instead of hoping a fixed pad was wide enough.

role: bootstrap (issue #515): `stemming:0.5` is the Charge panel's own floor — `adjustStemming` clamps at `Math.max(0.5, ...)` (Charge.ts) — the minimal stemming value reachable by any click sequence. `createCharge` (ChargePlan.ts) now enforces the same MIN_STEMMING_M floor (#527), so this step stays a `bootstrap` role for its `hole:*` batch shorthand, not to reach a value a player could not.
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

steps.command: zone clear x1:5 y1:5 x2:39 y2:39
steps.description: #557: evacuate the crew before firing. computeDangerZone(state.drillHoles, BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M) for this exact 2x2/spacing:4 grid at (20,20) pads out to (5,5)-(39,39), matching the literal box declared here -- the same rectangle Fire.ts's Sound the Horn button computes and sends. Both drillers (#1, #2) are parked exactly on the holes they just finished drilling (20,20) and (24,20), squarely inside it. Without this, Damage.ts's processProjections (attenuated out to the full 15m BLAST_DANGER_MARGIN_M, #557) kills both the instant the blast fires -- direct-traced: deathCount 0 -> 2, and with nobody left alive, payroll/maintenance stop accruing and every `cash should have decreased` checkpoint for the rest of this file reads a frozen figure instead. clearZone no longer teleports: this only orders a walkout, so the wait_until step right after is what proves it actually finished.

#557/#947: drain the real walkout Sound the Horn just ordered. #947 (this session's own fix): dropped the old `wait_until field:dangerZoneClear equals:true` -- both drillers (#1, #2) auto-dismount their drill_rigs (#1, #2) the instant each drilling task finishes, so both rigs are undriven by the time Sound the Horn fires here, and clearZone (Zone.ts) now refuses to even order a driverless vehicle out of the danger zone -- it reports it stranded instead, exactly the driving-itself-out-of-the-blast-zone bug #947 fixes. `dangerZoneClear` requires every vehicle AND every employee clear (isDangerZoneClear, Zone.ts), so with both rigs permanently stranded on their holes, that field can now never read true here -- a `wait_until` on it would stall the full `max_ticks` budget every run, so this is a plain tick pad instead (matching safety-projection-visual.json's #947 fix), split into tick/event pairs since command mode's own tick loop refuses to advance past a pending event. Both drillers (employees, not gated by #947) still walk out for real across this pad; only the driverless rigs stay behind. #947-followup (this fix): shrunk from `tick 100`x3 (300 ticks total) to `tick 20`x3 (60 ticks, matching safety-projection-visual.json's own #947 pad exactly) -- direct-traced live in interaction mode: the 300-tick version crashed wellBeing 53 -> 0 by tick 230 and triggered a genuine worker_revolt by tick 330, whose LevelEndScreen `.bs-confirm-overlay` is what actually covered the blast panel's execute button ("element is covered by div", CI's own reported symptom) -- not a stuck random-event dialog, so no amount of `resolveEventIfPending` could have closed it (the same misdiagnosis vibration-budget.json's own #707 correction already found once for this exact symptom). The two drillers only need to walk clear of the zone once, a short trip from either hole to open ground outside the (5,5)-(39,39) box; 60 ticks is ample margin over that and stays well clear of the wellBeing-crash/revolt threshold this file's own worker count and needs decay were tipping into.

expect.note: #947: dangerZoneClear reads false, not true -- both stranded driverless drill_rigs keep the zone permanently unclear now, a genuine new consequence of the #947 fix rather than a stale assumption to chase back to true. levelEnded stays false here (#947-followup): the shrunk 60-tick pad (see the first tick step's own note) keeps wellBeing off the worker_revolt threshold this file's original 300-tick pad crashed into live. The blast step's own `deathCount: 0` proof downstream is what actually shows the two drillers evacuated for real.

steps.description: Vibration from this blast dips Ecology and Nuisance immediately — the following checkpoints show them decaying back toward neutral while Safety/Well-being climb from the buildings above. #947-followup: leading `resolveEventIfPending` added -- the preceding step's own resolve and this step's first click are two separate real-time steps with a gap between them, and a timer event landing in that gap leaves its `.bs-confirm-overlay` covering the blast panel, failing this click with "element is covered by div" (same race rock-fragmenter-breaking.json's own #601-followup sequence/blast steps found and fixed, see their notes).

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace (command mode, seed:42): wellBeing/safety/ecology/nuisance all genuinely increase here, climbing from the two buildings and decaying back from the blast dip -- not asserted with increased on all four, since a real event firing under interaction mode's wall-clock ticking (Finding #12) can swing a score the opposite way (confirmed: a real browser run hit safety with a severe event penalty at this exact step) without the file's premise being wrong

steps.description: Resolved through the event dialog's own buttons. Decides whether an event is pending from authoritative game state, not from whether the modal has rendered -- a DOM-only probe silently missed events on a no-GPU runner where a frame costs ~6s, leaving them pending so later ticks halted and the run diverged while still passing command mode.
